dedupe_keys.name: building damage state mapping from strong motion after the 2023 turkey syria earthquake doublet

description: After the Mw 7.8 and Mw 7.5 earthquake doublet that struck south-eastern Türkiye on 6 February 2023, this study evaluated seismic damage across 11 provinces by analysing strong motion data, developing fragility functions and producing building damage state maps, validated against official reports and field surveys. Five idealised structural models with different fundamental periods represent typical Turkish structures, so the maps show how damage potential depends on building period. Coverage: 11 affected provinces. Access: open-access article in npj Natural Hazards (2025). Licence: CC-BY-4.0 article. Caveats: idealised models stand in for the real building stock, and damage validation relies on available official and field data. Outcome: near-fault damage was significantly underestimated by hazard maps from empirical ground motion models, since observed intensities far exceeded predictions within about 10 km of the rupture, and pulse-like motions, surface fault displacement and geohazards amplified damage. Simulation uses: rapid damage assessment from recorded motions and calibrating regional loss models for near-fault settings. Related records: the crowdsourced Turkey-Syria impact estimates and Pelicun.

name: Building damage state mapping from strong motion after the 2023 Turkey-Syria earthquake doublet
organisations: Guan Chen, Yong Liu, Zhangfeng Ma, Jiashu Yang and co-authors
outcomes: Damage state maps across 11 provinces showed how building period interacts with strong motion, and that near-fault damage within about 10 km was badly underestimated by hazard maps based on empirical ground motion models, pointing to tailored near-fault models.
resources_used: Strong motion records of the Mw 7.8 and Mw 7.5 events
Fragility functions for five idealised structural models
Official damage reports and field surveys for validation
